findings.text: Pole 1 of a genuine two-pole split, innocent, unwitting or hidden error: G0051's only citation (Heb 9:7) is explicitly the unintentional sins of the people, addressed through the sanctuary system, not moral failure in the culpable sense.

H7691 (Ps 19:12) is a direct plea about error the person cannot see in themselves (who can discern his errors? declare me innocent from hidden faults): error here is defined by its invisibility to the one who commits it.
H4879 (Job 19:4) is explicitly private and self-contained: my error remains with myself, offered as a defence that it harms no one else.
H8417 extends the category of error to a cosmic scale: even God's own angels he charges with error, relative to God's own standard (Job 4:18).

Pole 2 of the split, deliberate deception exercised as an act on someone else: G4106 (planē) is the richest single entry, ranging from fraud (the guards' report of a stolen body, Matt 27:64) to organized false teaching (Eph 4:14; 2 Thess 2:11's strong delusion; 1 John 4:6's spirit of error set against the Spirit of truth) to a term for entrenched moral corruption (Rom 1:27; Jude 11, Cain, Balaam and Korah as paradigm cases).

G1185 (deleazō) supplies the operative image for the deliberate pole: baiting a hook. Enticement works by appeal to his own desire (Jas 1:14) or sensual passions (2 Pet 2:18), that is, it succeeds through the target's own appetite, not force.
H8442 (Isa 32:6) folds error into a cluster with folly, iniquity and ungodliness: deliberate, not accidental.

The bridge case and the most consequential finding: H6601B (pathah) is morally bidirectional in its own verse set. Its 19 verses include straightforwardly negative enticement to sin: if sinners entice you (Prov 1:10), Job 31:9 and 27's self-indictment for a heart enticed toward a woman, and the plot against Samson (Judg 14:15).
findings.flag: Job 31:27 is given by number only and is not resolved to a verse

findings.text: H6601B (pathah) also names God's own tender wooing of Israel using the identical verb: I will allure her and speak tenderly to her (Hos 2:14).
H6601B (pathah) also appears in the heavenly-court scene where a spirit volunteers to entice Ahab to his death with God's own authorization (1 Kgs 22:20-22, repeated 2 Chr 18:19-21).
H6601B (pathah) also appears in Ezekiel 14:9's striking claim that God himself deceived a false prophet as an act of judgment.

On this evidence, entice and deceive (pathah) is not intrinsically a vice-word at its root: it names a persuasion-mechanism that the verses apply to seduction into sin, redemptive wooing and divine judicial deception alike, with the moral valence supplied entirely by context, not by the word.
